notes: Both agree that amino acids 157-165 of NTCP are critical determinants for viral receptor function. High overlap (5/6 claims shared: C74, C75, C76, C77, C93). Both cite the monkey-to-human NTCP domain swapping experiment as convincing evidence.

Both agree that NTCP knockdown experiments demonstrate NTCP is required for HBV/HDV infection. High overlap (8/9 claims shared: C41-C45, C47-C49). Both accept the RNAi evidence across multiple cell types and specificity controls.

Both agree that NTCP expression renders non-susceptible cells susceptible to HBV infection with authentic viral replication. Moderate overlap (8/9 LLM claims in peer set: C59-C66). Both accept cccDNA formation, kinetics, and dose-response data as convincing.

Both agree that NTCP expression confers HDV susceptibility to non-susceptible cells. Moderate overlap (6/8 LLM claims in peer set: C53-C58). Peer review encompasses both HDV (R2) and HBV (R3) gain-of-function data in their evaluation.

Both agree that NTCP is a functional receptor for HBV and HDV based on converging evidence. Moderate overlap (4/5 LLM claims in peer set: C14, C50, C86, C102). Both cite multiple independent lines of evidence as convincing.

Both express uncertainty about progeny virus production and infectivity. Moderate overlap (4/11 LLM claims in peer set: C70, C71, C72, C120). Both question whether low levels of infectious virions are produced and request additional data.

Both express uncertainty about infection efficiency, but focus on different aspects. Low overlap (2/11 LLM claims: C68, C69). LLM R8 addresses progeny virus production broadly; peer R6 specifically questions the 5-10% infection efficiency compared to PHH (C67).

LLM finds HBV infection data in HepG2-NTCP cells supported, while peer reviewers question the low infection efficiency (5-10%) and request comparison to PHH. Minimal overlap (1/9 claims: C67). Disagreement centers on whether infection efficiency data are adequately explained.

Both address NTCP identification, but with minimal claim overlap (1/15: C9). LLM R1 focuses on photo-cross-linking methodology and mass spectrometry identification. Peer R1 provides overall assessment of NTCP as receptor based on multiple evidence types. Semantic alignment on NTCP identification despite different claim groupings.

Both address NTCP expression dynamics, but minimal overlap (1/4 claims: C46). LLM R7 focuses on temporal decrease in cultured hepatocytes correlating with viral susceptibility loss. Peer R2 includes C46 as part of knockdown evidence. Semantic connection through NTCP expression but different analytical focus.
